We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={t}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=2t, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=3{e}^{2t+2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int 3{e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t=\frac{3}{2}{e}^{2t+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{t}^{2}{e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =({t}^{2})(\frac{3}{2}{e}^{2t+2})-\int (\frac{3}{2}{e}^{2t+2})(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}{e}^{2t+2}-3\int t{e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int t{e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=1, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{2t+2}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t{e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t)(\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t+2})-\int (\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t+2})(1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}t{e}^{2t+2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}t{e}^{2t+2}-\frac{1}{4}{e}^{2t+2}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{t}^{2}{e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}{e}^{2t+2}-3\int t{e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}{e}^{2t+2}-3(\frac{1}{2}t{e}^{2t+2}-\frac{1}{4}{e}^{2t+2}+D) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}{e}^{2t+2}-\frac{3}{2}t{e}^{2t+2}+\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2t+2}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-3D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}3{t}^{2}{e}^{2t+2}\,\text{d}t & =(\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}{e}^{2t+2}-\frac{3}{2}t{e}^{2t+2}+\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2t+2})\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{3}{2}({1}^{2}){e}^{2(1)+2}-\frac{3}{2}(1){e}^{2(1)+2}+\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2(1)+2})-(\frac{3}{2}({0}^{2}){e}^{2(0)+2}-\frac{3}{2}(0){e}^{2(0)+2}+\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2(0)+2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{e}^{4}-\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{4}-3{e}^{2}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
